[[9 ABY]]{{SkeletonCrewDate}} {{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2024/08/star-wars-skeleton-crew-trailer-1236036313/|text='Star Wars: Skeleton Crew' First Trailer Shows Jude Law As Jedi|author=Anthony D'Alessandro, Katie Campione|date=2024-08-09|archivedate=20241230171000}} establishes [[Wim]] was around ten years old during the events of ''Skeleton Crew'', meaning he must have been [[Reproduction|born]] around [[1 BBY]], and {{InsiderCite|232|Wim's World: Ravi Cabot-Conyers}} establishes Wim's [[Parent|mother]] [[Death|passed away]] before the events of the series. |species= |gender=[[Gender|Female]]{{SkeletonCrew|This Could Be a Real Adventure}} |pronouns=She/her{{InsiderCite|232|Wim's World: Ravi Cabot-Conyers}} |height= |mass= |hair= |feathers= |eyes= |skin= |cyber= |families= |parents= |partners=[[Wendle]] {{C|co-[[parent]]}} |siblings= |children=[[Wim]] |affiliation= |masters= |apprentices= }} {{Quote|Will you please read me a story like Mom used to?|Wim, to his father|}} A [[Gender|female]] individual was the '''mother''' of the [[human]] boy [[Wim]], who was born around [[1 BBY]] and lived on the [[planet]] [[At Attin]]. She read stories to Wim, and by around [[9 ABY]], she had [[Death|died]]. Around that [[Standard year|year]], Wim asked his [[Parent|father]], [[Wendle]], to read him a story like his mother had, but Wendle refused. Wim later spoke about his parents with the [[pirate]] [[Jod Na Nawood]], who told him that he would see them again soon. The boy responded that that was not true of his mother, and Na Nawood then advised Wim to forget his parents. ==Biography== {{Quote|I—I miss my dad. And my mom.''"
"''Chin up. You'll see 'em again soon.''"
"''Not my mom.|Wim and Jod Na Nawood|}} [[File:Wim-MP.png|thumb|right|225px|The woman read stories to their son, Wim (pictured).]] A [[Gender|female]] individual was the [[Parent|mother]] of [[Wim]], a [[human]] boy from the [[planet]] [[At Attin]]—which was separated from the rest of [[the galaxy]] by the [[Barrier]]—who was [[Reproduction|born]] around [[1 BBY]]. The individual read stories to Wim, and by around [[9 ABY]], she had [[Death|passed away]]. Around that [[Standard year|year]], in his [[Wim's home|home]] on At Attin, when Wim felt that he was unable to [[sleep]], he asked his father, [[Wendle]], to read a story to him like his mother used to. However, Wendle stated he needed to work and added that Wim was getting too old for bedtime stories. Later, Wim and a [[Skeleton Crew|group]] of other [[Youngling|children]] discovered the [[starship]] ''[[Onyx Cinder]]''{{SkeletonCrew|You Have a Lot to Learn About Pirates}} and became lost after accidentally causing it to jump to [[hyperspace]]. The children eventually allied themselves with the [[pirate]] [[Jod Na Nawood]] and traveled to the planet [[Lanupa]], where they hoped to find At Attin's coordinates so they could [[Mission to At Attin|return]] there. On the way, Na Nawood found Wim sitting on the floor of the ship. Wim admitted that although he had wanted an adventure, it was different than he expected, and that he missed both his mother and father. Na Nawood told Wim that he would see them again soon and then began walking away, but Wim responded he would not see his mother. The pirate then sat with Wim and advised him to forget his fears, anxieties, and parents, claiming he did not need attachments, but Wim said he could not do so. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|I would journal in the mind of Wim. I mostly wrote about his mom, because we don't know much about her. I enjoyed imagining what Wim's life was like before she passed away. Jon didn't give us too many details about her, because he wanted me to figure that out for myself.|Ravi Cabot-Conyers|}} Wim's mother was first mentioned in "[[This Could Be a Real Adventure]]," the first episode of the live-action [[Disney+]] series ''[[Star Wars: Skeleton Crew]]'',{{SW|url=series/skeleton-crew/season-1-episode-1-episode-guide|text="This Could Be a Real Adventure" Episode Guide | Star Wars: Skeleton Crew}} which aired on [[December 2]], [[2024]].{{SW|url=news/skeleton-crew-premiere-date|text=''Star Wars: Skeleton Crew'' Will Debut Early|date=2024-11-26}} [[Ravi Cabot-Conyers]], who portrayed Wim, often journaled in the character's mind, mostly writing about his mother because little was known about her. Cabot-Conyers said he enjoyed imagining what Wim's life was like before she passed away and that showrunner [[Jon Watts]] did not give Cabot-Conyers many details about Wim's mother, as he wanted him to figure them out for himself. In one journal entry, Cabot-Conyers theorized that Wim's mother had fueled his zest for adventure and that he missed making crafts with her. He also complimented Wim's optimistic outlook toward [[the galaxy]], believing that it served as escapism from being a motherless child, as well as from boredom and attachments. However, Cabot-Conyers also believed that Wim did get very attached, such as to his family and to a mobile his mother made him. ==Appearances== *{{SkeletonCrew|This Could Be a Real Adventure}} {{1stm}} *{{SkeletonCrew|You Have a Lot to Learn About Pirates}} {{Mo}} ==Sources== *{{InsiderCite|232|Wim's World: Ravi Cabot-Conyers}} ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |fr=Mère de Wim |ka=უიმის დედა }} [[Category:At Attin residents]] [[Category:Females]] [[Category:Individuals of unspecified species]] [[Category:Individuals with she/her pronouns]]
